turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

Let me examine which compositions achieve the highest Tc in the dataset.

**Top performers (excluding H2S which is a pressure-stabilized outlier):**
- Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 → **132 K**
- Ba2Ca2Cu3O → **126 K**
- Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O → **120.2 K**
- Tl1Ba1Ca1Cu2O5.5 → **114 K**
- Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 → **110 K**
- Bi1.4Pb0.5Sb0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O → **109 K**
- Cu4.5V0.5Sr2Ca1O → **107 K**
- Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O → **105.7 K**

**Key patterns:** The champions are all **cuprates** — they universally contain **O, Cu, Ca**, plus **Ba/Sr** and often **Bi/Pb/Tl**. The highest Tc (132 K) is the Hg-Ba-Ca-Cu-O family. Among available design variables, the winning recipe features:

- **High O** — all top performers are oxides
- **Substantial Cu** — the superconducting CuO₂ planes
- **Ca** near max — Ca between CuO₂ planes boosts Tc (3-layer cuprates)
- **Ba** present (Hg-1223 uses Ba2)
- **Bi and Pb** — appear in many >100 K compounds (Bi-2223)
- **Sr** — appears in Tl/Bi families

Elements like Fe, As, Nb, C, B, Mo, V, Zn, Ni, Y, La, Pr, Ce tend to appear in **lower-Tc** materials (Fe-pnictides ~30-50 K, borides/carbides ~10-40 K, Y-based cuprates ~90 K but not the highest). Ce/Pr often **suppress** Tc. Y is actually beneficial (YBCO ~90 K) but the very top is Hg/Bi/Tl-Ba-Ca-Cu-O.

# Strategy

Maximize the cuprate-defining elements (O, Cu, Ca, Ba, Sr) and add Bi/Pb which characterize the 100+ K Bi-based phases. Keep suppressive/off-family elements (Fe, As, Nb, B, Mo, V, Zn, Ni, C, Ce, Pr, Y, La) at or near zero.

- O → max (0.697674) — oxide framework
- Cu → max (0.454545) — CuO₂ planes
- Ca → max (0.272727) — interlayer, 3-layer stacking
- Ba → max (0.333333) — Hg-1223 family
- Sr → max (0.285714) — Bi/Tl family
- Bi → high — Bi-2223 (110 K)
- Pb → moderate — Pb doping enhances Bi phases
- All others → 0
